question: Compare charging by contact and charging by induction. In which method does the charging body lose some of its charge? Give reason.

options.A: In contact, there is no transfer of charge; in induction there is direct contact. The charging body loses charge in induction.
options.B: Both methods require direct contact; the charging body loses charge equally in both methods.
options.C: Induction transfers charge by direct touch, while contact acts only by influence. The charging body loses charge in neither method.
options.D: In contact, charge is transferred by touching, so the charging body loses some charge. In induction, charging occurs without contact through redistribution and the charging body does not lose charge.
